Oh nvm, they've already been banned and the messages weren't deleted. <@403707149043105803> I think we missed something in context of EOF and 31-byte chunking. The 1 byte prefix is only needed to runtime check the jump target. This is not needed in EOF. We will know where to start executing a chunk based on the previous instruction. I.e. EOF can pack code into 32-byte chunks. 🎉 🥳 Yup, we discussed this at Edelweiss 🙂 The only improvement we could make is interleaving code/type headers to reduce the number of header chunks in case of subset of functions are needed. My takeaway from today is that we could also go over what header values are required at runtime for what opcodes and consider verkle-optimizing the format for to make them more local example is CALLF currently requires at time: - offset to start target execution - target's max_stack_height - target's number of inputs - offset potentially could be put into CALLF's immediate instead of target index - max_stack_height and inputs potentially could be put in front of target section code instead of header

excerpts.content:
example is CALLF currently requires at time:
- offset to start target execution
- target's max_stack_height
- target's number of inputs

- offset potentially could be put into CALLF's immediate instead of target index
- max_stack_height and inputs potentially could be put in front of target section code instead of header
